question: What is a stack, and how does a monotonic stack find the next greater element?

scenes.sub: Keep a pile of unanswered questions. A bigger arrival answers many at once.
scenes.say: A stack is the simplest structure, yet it solves a whole class of next bigger problems in linear time.

scenes.head: Think of a stack of plates

items.label: Stack
items.sub: you only touch the top plate

scenes.say: A stack is like a pile of plates. You only touch the top one. Now picture people in a line, each waiting to see someone taller to their right. The waiting people pile up on a stack. When a tall newcomer arrives, they answer every shorter person on top.

scenes.head: Next greater element of [2, 1, 2, 4, 3]
scenes.say: Array two, one, two, four, three. For each, find the next bigger number to its right. Walk left to right with a stack of waiting positions. Two arrives. Push it. One arrives. Smaller, so it waits too. Now two arrives. It beats one, so pop one, answer two. Push two. Four arrives. It beats the two, and the other two. Both answers are four. Push four. Three arrives. Push it. Anyone left has no bigger number, so minus one.

scenes.head: The same stack checks brackets
scenes.say: The same stack checks brackets. The last one opened must be the first one closed, like nested boxes. Push every opener. On a closer, the top must be its partner, otherwise false. At the end, the stack must be empty. Also try Daily Temperatures, Largest Rectangle in Histogram, and Trapping Rain Water.

scenes.head: In the interview
rows: Why O of n with a while inside a for?
Each index is pushed once and popped once.
Flip the comparison, or scan from the right.
Indices. You can read the value, and compute distances.
Forgetting leftovers: they have no answer.
scenes.say: Why O of n with a while inside a for? Each index is pushed once and popped once. Next smaller, or previous greater? Flip the comparison, or scan from the right. Stack of values or indices? Indices. Common mistake: forgetting leftovers, which have no answer.

lines: A stack is last in, first out.
Monotonic stack: pop everything the new element beats, and answer them.
Each index is pushed and popped once: O(n).
scenes.say: A stack is last in, first out. A monotonic stack pops everything the new element beats, and answers them. Each index is pushed and popped once, so it's O of n.
